doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Writing and recording his tune 'Why Not'
summary: After a playback of 'Why Not', Person explains the tune just came to him, he usually plays others' songs, and it won awards.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All right. I wanted to play a little cut off one of your fairly recent numbers, and ask you just a little bit about this. [audio interlude: selection “Why Not” composed by Houston Person]
That’s some great stuff. Can you relate how this tune or most tunes come to you? How do you write?
Come on. You can tell me. You know, is it divine inspiration?

Well yeah. Because I usually like to play other people’s music and this one, it just came to me and it fit and there was a bridge I put in there, and I say, oh you never play your own stuff. Then I say why not? So that’s where the title came from.
I mean some people have told me that they would put on a tune even if it was a simple little blues head, because they would get some writer’s royalties out of it.
But that doesn’t seem to be your motivation.
No. No I usually do other people’s tunes. I like that. And I usually try to give these songs to other guys. But I’m glad I did this one. It won some awards. So I was happy about that.
